item.title: Explore Britain's Hidden Archaeology
item.summary: This is a LiDAR view of Stonehenge. The image also shows the extensive Normanton Down Barrow Cemetery, where dozens of Bronze Age burial mounds are scattered across the surrounding landscape. Look closely and you can also make out the Avenue, a prehistoric earthwork consisting of parallel banks and ditches that once provided a formal approach to Stonehenge. This is just one example of the extraordinary archaeological detail revealed by LiDAR Lens - Great Britain . The interactive map uses high-resolution LiDAR elevation data to expose subtle features in the landscape that are often invisible in conventional maps and aerial photographs. Using a circular lens, you can explore the terrain through different visualisation techniques, including hillshade, slope, local relief and sky-view factor. These reveal everything from ancient burial mounds and earthworks to abandoned field systems and historic landscape features. To get started with LiDAR Lens you can explore these interesting locations: Stonehenge Avebury Stone Circle Silbury Hill Maiden Castle Uffington White Horse Each offers a different landscape to investigate, and switching between the visualisation options can reveal details

item.title: The Never-Ending Coastline
item.summary: Today's 30DayMapChallenge task is Borgesian Map – a map so detailed it becomes the territory. The challenge takes its inspiration from Jorge Luis Borges' short story On Exactitude in Science , in which cartographers create a map so accurate and detailed that it eventually becomes the same size as the empire it represents. For my contribution, I've created The Never-Ending Coastline , an interactive map exploring one of cartography's most intriguing curiosities: the coastline paradox . How long is a coastline? It sounds like a straightforward geographical question, but the answer depends entirely on how closely you look. My map illustrates this using three different versions of the same stretch of coastline. At the first level, we trace the broad outline, smoothing over small bays, inlets and headlands. Zoom in and we capture more of the shoreline's twists and turns. Zoom in again and we discover yet more detail, producing an even longer coastline. As you scroll through the map, each successive level reveals a more detailed version of the same shore. The map zooms in as the resolution increases, while the measured coastline grows longer. At each stage, the polyline can be gradually

#30DayMapChallenge Day 13 - Interactive

4 for the price of 1 today.  Just to show you how easy it is....  Instead of creating one interactive map, Cadence and AI created 4 dashboards covering the following topics, all using in-built trusted data and in-built trusted calculations:

- Stats19 explorer (see video)
- A grid carbon intensity explorer
- A house price and house sales explorer
- A street crime explorer

As well as amazing maps, charts and stories, Cadence dashboards and our ever-growing curated databank let you create trusted bits of analysis in minutes, which can be shared online with colleagues and friends with a single click. Alternatively, pull your QGIS data in using our QGIS connector and create your interactive online dashboard from that.
